title: Vesper MedTech — product portfolio
decision_question: Should Vesper MedTech discontinue its low reported-margin sterile connector C and redeploy the team to connector D?

initial_hypothesis.statement: Drop connector C immediately because it has 8% reported product gross margin versus 30% for D.
initial_hypothesis.explanation: C has high direct contribution despite allocated overhead; an immediate exit loses cash contribution and triggers contractual penalties. Redesign or an orderly future sunset is more defensible.

key_insights.text: C generates $3.8M direct contribution on $6M sales, despite an 8.3% reported margin after $3.3M shared allocation.
Immediate C exit with the maximum D transfer changes annual operating contribution by $-2.65M before contract penalties; first year $-4.75M.
Only $0.4M of C allocated overhead is avoidable; shared regulatory and depreciation costs do not simply disappear.
Nine customer bundles require C, with $2.1M first-year penalties and 95% bundle service requirement.
Redesign could save $1.25M annually for $0.55M one time, subject to customer validation and implementation.
Renewal gap is not causal evidence because C accounts are older, smaller and less-supported.

required_calculations.text: Exit annual net impact (optimistic D transfer)
One-year net redesign benefit before time phasing

decision_relevant_evidence.text: Direct-variable costs versus allocated shared costs
Nine bundle contracts and $2.1M exit penalty
D substitution limited to $1.5M incremental revenue
Bundle-level service definition and patient device validation

contradictory_evidence: C gross margin is allocated operating metric, not incremental contribution
C customers renew less but differ in size and support
Item-level service dashboard hides whole-bundle delays

reasoning_traps.text: Equating a low allocated margin with negative avoidable contribution
Assuming all shared overhead is saved on exit
Treating C ownership as a cause of lower renewal

plausible_recommendations.text: Retain C for now, fix bundle service and test the $0.55M redesign, then reconsider sunset when contracts renew.
Pursue a negotiated phased exit if customer consents and new capacity/transfer economics establish positive value.
Discontinue C immediately based only on the 8% reported margin.

defensibility_criteria: Reconcile margins to avoidable cash flows
Apply contract penalty separately from annual cost
Bound D substitution with capacity and validation
Avoid causal inference from account-mix correlation

decision_requirements.question: Are product costs classified by avoidability?
Is D substitution backed by realistic capacity and qualification?
Is the comparison more than reported gross margin?
